editorial.summary: Day Six begins with fatigue, a suspected-but-unproven restaurant rejection and a freight ride framed by an explicit sexual/racial text performance and David's admittedly uncertain account of Chinese railroad labor. Luis recounts a friend's train amputation, refuses a dangerous train and is immediately pressured to drink and board; David later issues a disclaimer while calling himself a professional. At the Canadian border, David says a youth record blocks entry, an attempted forest crossing triggers enforcement and tapes are confiscated. A hostile anti-Canada song is followed by a next-day apology and responsibility, then more proposed evasion routes. Bernadette and Jerry are treated as competing hitchhikers before David yields the spot. At Taildraggers, David repeatedly overrides Grant's denials and privacy by inferring sexual orientation from appearance, disclosing an absent pregnant partner's sexuality and inventing a gay-pilot etymology. An acoustically unverified Andrew line precedes the claim of a flight around Canada. Every idea remains in the source; the editorial layer keeps uncertainty, contradiction, private identity, third-party disclosure, legal context and publisher labels separate.

source_notes.claim: Chinese laborers used distinctive dangerous methods and made these train lines after railroad construction fell behind.
source_notes.assessment: Chinese workers were indispensable to the western portion of the first transcontinental railroad and were systematically minimized in later histories. The episode's broad hiring rationale, techniques and 'all these lines' wording remain compressed and partly unsupported.

source_notes.claim: Youth graffiti and shoplifting records should disappear in America but caused permanent Canadian exclusion.
source_notes.assessment: Canadian admissibility depends on the offence, disposition, whether someone was treated as a young offender or adult, time and rehabilitation. Canada states that some people convicted under 18 may still enter; the episode's personal outcome does not establish a universal rule.
Correct public fact; it does not validate the surrounding sexual stereotypes or claimed flight.
